questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/936cea1e20ef7bbc1eb66acf9dd564c61476f5bb68ee05e553b00aaf3f970dc3.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible? 

I. $x\in [-4,0]$

II. $x\in (-4,-2]$

III. $x\in (-3,1)$
questions.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.  

- The given function is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in [-4,0]$ and $x\in (-4,-2].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/a4499c2d4995c09b9ab6f8852cc2982f415f1650d65429c86df83800344106f4.png)

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $x\in (-3,1]$  because some lines will intersect the curve at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/cb0a462b3af10d15bb586f127baac45a74eecd5dc19848bda23664e75de968a4.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=|x-1|-2,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

I. $x\in (-\infty ,1]$

II. $x\in (1,\infty )$

III. $x\in (-\infty ,2]$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=|x-1|-2$ can be obtained in the following way:

1\. Take the curve $y=|x|.$

2\. Translate it by $1$ units to the right,  to get $y=|x-1|.$

3\. Finally, translate $y=|x-1|$ by $2$ units down to get $f(x)=|x-1|-2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/753840da17642582f9dbc0debc18f1fa3efcbbb11142894c1dd823ad6c0c630a.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-\infty ,1]$ and $x\in (1,\infty ).$ On these intervals, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/15f1c797cbddd2ac8e2e9c5be72f842e7d1accfc5f619af57b1f35a27e1015c0.png)

  

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,2].$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/a100489b49da7b06c98783b1b1c4ec0de9d891fc2b22f4b36b1a0ac2d54fc4f3.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I  and II only".
